subject: Request: incident evidence escrow, IRP artifacts, and SIG/CAIQ mapping
messages:
From: Ava Lin <ava.lin@finserv.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Request: incident evidence escrow + IRP artifacts and SIG/CAIQ mapping

Marissa,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. Per our procurement and security teams: Orchard Bank needs a compact evidence bundle from the recent auth spike on 2028-10-28 for our internal SIG review and to satisfy a scheduled SOC 2 audit. Specifically we need:

- A short incident timeline (UTC) and root-cause summary
- Forensic export (anonymized where required) with auth logs, token traces, and service metrics for 10/28–10/29
- A mapping document tying artifacts to SIG and CAIQ control IDs

Can you confirm: delivery format, redaction approach, expected ETA, and whether Redwood can temporarily escrow the bundle on an SFTP for audit review? Also flag if anything here will need an exception / legal sign-off.

For context: we are under a compliance window and need the bundle available to our auditor by 2028-11-06. If you need a PO or forms, loop me in.

Thanks,
Ava Lin
Security & Vendor Risk
Orchard Bank

---
Attachment: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Lin <ava.lin@finserv.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: incident evidence escrow + IRP artifacts and SIG/CAIQ mapping

Ava —

Appreciate the summary and deadline. We can produce an evidence bundle and a SIG/CAIQ mapping. High-level plan:

1) Incident timeline and brief root-cause (PDF) — prepared by me and security ops; targeted delivery: 2028-11-02 18:00 UTC.
2) Forensic export (tar.gz) — sanitized exports containing auth logs, service traces, and aggregated metrics. We will remove any customer PII and redact tokens; expected delivery to a temporary SFTP: 2028-11-03 04:00 UTC.
3) SIG/CAIQ mapping (XLSX + CSV) — Neha will map artifacts to common control IDs and call out anything that is partial or not applicable: delivery 2028-11-03 12:00 UTC.

We will hold the bundle on an SFTP for 14 days by default; if you need a different retention window let us know. To proceed we need:
- SFTP endpoint credentials or preferred upload method (if your auditor needs direct access we can set a read-only account)
- Any redaction rules you require beyond PII (e.g., card numbers, masked IPs)

I will also mark this as an internal IR and run the postmortem draft by legal for any sensitive wording — I don’t anticipate a formal NDA but we can route one quickly if required.

Jonas/Neha — can you confirm the export scope and whether we need Forensix involvement for the raw disk-level artifacts?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Trust & Security Ops
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: incident_timeline_v1.pdf (stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Lin <ava.lin@finserv.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: incident evidence escrow + IRP artifacts and SIG/CAIQ mapping

Marissa —

Scope confirmation from infra/forensics side: we will include the following in the forensic export (sanitized):
- auth_service logs (10/28 00:00 UTC -> 10/29 23:59 UTC) aggregated and per-tenant slices
- token issuance and validation traces (with token IDs replaced by hash placeholders)
- sidecar telemetry and host-level metrics for affected cluster nodes
- relevant config snapshots and deploy diffs (if present in the window)

We do not plan to include raw disk images unless the customer explicitly requests and signs an authorization for forensic level access — that triggers a separate workflow with Forensix for chain-of-custody.

Ava — please confirm the SFTP hostname and whether we should create a temporary user (recommended) or push a signed presigned URL. For redaction: we will redact any 16-digit sequences and full IPs if you request; otherwise we will mask last octet.

ETA looks good on our side. I’ll stage the export to /orchardbank/20281101-forensic_export.tar.gz (stub) on our SFTP and email creds once ready.

-Jonas
Senior Incident Response
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: incident evidence escrow + IRP artifacts and SIG/CAIQ mapping

Ava —

I’ve started the SIG/CAIQ crosswalk. Deliverables: a short mapping spreadsheet (SIG control -> artifact name -> evidence path) and a CAIQ matrix that marks coverage and notes. Preliminary notes:
- Auth logging and token traces map to SIG sections SIG.AI-Authentication and CAIQ AC-5/AC-7 coverage; I’ll flag controls where we provide aggregated logs vs. raw event streams.
- Control exceptions: where telemetry retention policies exclude raw payloads we’ll mark as N/A and include a compensating control (e.g., aggregated metrics + alert traces).

I’ll upload a working copy to the shared drive and attach a final XLSX in the bundle. Expect the mapping by 2028-11-03 12:00 UTC.

Link (working copy): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-external-evidence-bundle

-Neha
Security Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Marissa/Team —

Thank you, that plan is reasonable. A couple of clarifications before you deliver:

1) Redaction: please redact full primary account numbers and mask full client IPs (mask last octet is fine).
2) Auditor access: we prefer a read-only SFTP account for the auditor (name: Deloitte_FS_Audit). Can you create that user and share credentials to me only?
3) Chain of custody: we will accept the sanitized tar.gz for the auditor but will request disk-level artifacts only if our auditor identifies a gap; If that’s needed, Forensix will coordinate.

PO will follow from procure@orchardbank.com by EOD. ETA target (11/03) is acceptable.

Ava
